dateFinding.epistemic: Observed for isIsoDate (its exact text, run); Inferred for the consent reader's line (rebuilt from its exact text, not run in place)
dateFinding.claim: act-fields isIsoDate accepts calendar dates that do not exist, because it checks the shape and then asks Date.parse, which V8 answers for them; the consent package reader refuses the same strings by a round trip through toISOString. The two authorities decide differently on these date-only strings.

validators.how: the function itself, from its exact text
rebuilt from the line: finite parse, then the round trip to the same day
validators.exactText:
const day = Date.parse(`${date}T00:00:00Z`);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(day) || new Date(day).toISOString().slice(0, 10) !== date

validators.how: the function itself, from its exact text

rebuilt from the lines: whole seconds with Z, the same day as the stated date, finite parse, round trip to the same text

dateFinding.reach: isIsoDate is the date test of the act-instant and expires checks in body-read-authority.ts and walkthrough-judgment.ts (class 1). Not changed here: tightening it changes what a gate accepts, an owner decision (GP-Q0).
